import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    postings = inputs["postings"].copy()

    # Preserve original column order/types; sort per legacy cursor order
    postings = postings.sort_values(
        by=["account_id", "post_date", "post_seq"],
        kind="mergesort"  # stable sort to mimic deterministic cursor order
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Determine validity of each row per the legacy TRY block logic
    qty = postings["qty"]
    price = postings["unit_price"]

    valid = (
        qty.notna()
        & (qty > 0)
        & price.notna()
        & (price >= 0)
    )

    postings["_valid"] = valid
    postings["post_value"] = qty * price

    # Running total: cumulative sum of post_value only over valid rows, per account
    # Invalid rows do not contribute and do not appear in output, but running_total
    # must reflect only prior valid rows within the same account.
    valid_rows = postings[postings["_valid"]].copy()
    valid_rows["running_total"] = valid_rows.groupby("account_id")["post_value"].cumsum()

    posted_totals = valid_rows[
        ["account_id", "post_seq", "post_date", "post_value", "running_total"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    # Reject counts: per account, count of invalid rows; include accounts with zero rejects
    all_accounts = postings["account_id"].drop_duplicates()
    reject_per_row = postings[~postings["_valid"]]
    reject_counts_series = reject_per_row.groupby("account_id").size()

    reject_counts = all_accounts.to_frame(name="account_id")
    reject_counts["reject_count"] = reject_counts["account_id"].map(reject_counts_series).fillna(0).astype(int)

    # Preserve the order of first appearance of account_id (as in cursor iteration)
    reject_counts = reject_counts.reset_index(drop=True)

    return {
        "posted_totals": posted_totals,
        "reject_counts": reject_counts,
    }
